baseline_note: Current law, 2027–2031, all building sizes, from the shared all-housing baseline (the same for every pairing). It includes a small statewide adjustment not assigned to any place.
double_count: Both reforms make it easier to build apartments near frequent transit. A building that goes ahead because the law allows more height and also because it no longer needs a parking garage would be counted once by each reform's estimate. Adding the two estimates near stops counts it twice. Away from stops only the parking reform acts, so there is nothing to double count and the two are simply added.
headline: b

headline_reason.text: Why the larger of the two is the headline: California's AB 2097 removed parking minimums near major transit in 2023. In Los Angeles, where transit areas had already been upzoned, it brought no measurable gain in homes permitted beyond what parking relief brought elsewhere in California (the difference was −2.62 homes a year per 1,000 existing homes, 90% interval −6.07 to +0.98). So there is no evidence that the two reforms add up near stops.

roles.tod_label: Central: the average district place, across about 12% of lots within ¼ mile of transit
Upper: scaled to 15% of lots within ¼ mile of transit

rounding_note: Each figure is rounded on its own, so columns may differ from sums by one home.
rule_c: A third reading, adding both and then subtracting the overlap measured in cities that did both reforms, is a sensitivity case only and has no number yet. The cities that could measure it differ from Wisconsin and from each other: New York kept its parking minimums near transit, while Charlotte, Chicago and Saint Paul cut them, in different markets and decades.

a.info: Near stops, both reforms' additions are added. A new building that both reforms would count is counted twice, so this is an upper bound, not an equal alternative.
a.label: Upper bound if the two reforms' effects simply add

b.info: Near stops, each place gets whichever reform adds more there in that year, as if the smaller effect were already inside the larger. A reform estimated to reduce homes is subtracted in full, never set to zero. This is the headline.
b.label: Both laws together (larger of the two near stops)
